tier_reason: First-party only: README Performance table (encode median 0.96x, N=41, z -3.59; decode median 1.02x, N=31, z -0.18) and WHYS.md/CHANGES.md logs against FFmpeg 8.1.2 -threads 1, but the paired.ps1/paired2.ps1/pinned.ps1 harness is not in the repo (examples/ holds only decode_bench.rs and other single-binary tools), and no CPU model or rustc flags are stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No speedup: README states parity with FFmpeg 8.1.2. Encode median 0.96x (paired interleaved, N=41, z -3.59, matched output size with ours 3.1% smaller); decode median 1.02x (WHYS.md: 15/31, z -0.18, median 1.0157, inside noise). WHYS.md gives the ratio as FFmpeg time over ours, so encode is about 4% slower and decode about 2% faster within noise. WHYS.md shows the same encode comparison reading 1.4510 at N=15, 1.0286 at N=21 and 0.9608 at N=41; CHANGES.md withdraws the earlier 1.19-1.45x claims of 0.1.x to 0.2.x as small-N artifacts, and the earlier 'decode 1.04x faster' was N=15.
corrections.caveats: Not faster than the baseline: the project's own final standing is parity, and its encode test (N=41) reads about 4% slower. Threads: one pinned core each and ffmpeg -threads 1, but WHYS.md D6f records that the 'single-threaded' arm was silently multithreaded (decoder.rs hard-coded PreferWorkerKind::Multithreaded) until repaired, and an earlier 'decode 1.17x faster' reading came entirely from extra cores. Timer is pinned CPU time; decode bitstream and per-frame checksums are identical across arms, while encode outputs differ (matched size only, ours 3.1% smaller; no output-quality comparison at matched size). Reproducibility is poor: the PowerShell harness scripts (pinned.ps1, paired.ps1, paired2.ps1) named in WHYS.md are not in the repo tree, CPU model and rustc settings are missing (Cargo.toml has no release profile; MSRV 1.85), and the author notes the box drifts about 15% and that the same ffmpeg command drifted 953 to 1266 ms within one session. FFmpeg's native MJPEG codec is a different baseline from libjpeg-turbo. WHYS.md also documents several void measurements and a trellis cost claim off by 46x (CHANGES.md: trellis was +144% encode time on real footage, not +3.1%). The crate is a vendored merge of jpeg-decoder 0.3.2 (image-rs) and jpeg-encoder 0.7.0 (vstroebel, already in the catalog at tier D) with its own AVX2/NEON kernels, fused decode-IDCT and mask-driven AC scan; not a GitHub fork. The '2,784 active installs' figure is a first-party README badge (RAG Converter, WebAssembly). Kept as a flagged entry.

notes: Parity verified in README, WHYS.md (Standing table, lines ~1340-1360) and CHANGES.md; confirm at C as a not-faster flagged entry per orchestrator. jpeg-encoder (vstroebel) is a separate catalog entry; rusty_jpeg carries substantial own SIMD work, so not marked duplicate. Repo: 1 star, 0 forks, 38 commits, last commit 2026-10-04, license (MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND IJG.

corrections.caveats: No numeric comparison against any recognizable baseline: perf.png is a table that compares boards with each other (speed rating relative to Cortex-M0+, plus current draw), with no libgif or giflib column. The 2-30x claim is Turbo versus the library's own Normal mode, with no table, harness, compiler, flags or image set behind it; examples/gif_benchmark/gif_benchmark.ino (an Arduino sketch timing one mode with micros()) says Turbo 'will usually result in a nearly 2X speedup' and has no libgif arm. README says the library performs far better than libgif on PC-class devices but gives no figure; the wiki (single Home page) has no numbers, linux/ holds only a Makefile (-O2) and examples, and MacOS/GIF_Test is an Xcode project with no results. Author's blog post 'A Big Memory GIF Decoder' is blocked here. Same Turbo LZW technique as the already-listed giflib-turbo (same author), which carries the drop-in giflib comparison. Tier D kept for the record; the project is notable (537 stars, 76 forks).
